text.p: Australian December quarter inflation data will be released at 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT) today.

Forecasts for the consumer price index (CPI), or headline rate of inflation, centre on a 0.3 percent rise in the quarter and an annual rate of 1.6 percent. Quarterly CPI forecasts range from a rise of 0.1 to 0.5 percent, leading to annual inflation rate forecasts of between 1.4 and 1.9 percent.

For the key underlying rate, forecasts centre on a quarterly rise of 0.4 percent, to be 2.1 percent higher over the year. Quarterly forecasts range from rises of 0.2 to 0.7 percent, leading to annual forecasts of 1.9 to 2.3 percent.
Recent data and December quarter forecasts are below.
If the data comes in as forecast, it will be the lowest annual CPI reading since the March quarter 1994, and the underlying rate will be at its lowest level since the March 1995 quarter.
The moderation in the CPI largely reflects the impact of the first cut in official interest rates on July 31, flowing through to consumers in the form of lower mortgage and loan repayments.
Further moderation in the CPI is expected during 1997, possibly to under 1.0 percent, as the imapct of the November and December rate cuts is felt.

Economists said the underlying rate, which is the focus of monetary policy, will reflect the rise of the Australian dollar through 1996, continued subdued growth in partial price indicator series as well as only moderate wages growth.
The Reserve Bank targets the underlying inflation rate, aiming to keep it to an average of between two and three percent over a run of years.
The expectations of favourable inflation data today were boosted by the downward revisions to inflation forecasts in the government's mid year review released on Tuesday.

For the 1996/97 year to June 30 forecasts for year-average underlying inflation were lowered to 2.0 percent from the 2.75 percent published in the August budget. The year-average consumer price index forecast was lowered to 1.5 percent from an original 2.0 percent forecast.

Economists surveyed by Reuters generally expect the annual underlying rate to trough in the June quarter of this year, at just under 2.0 percent, before gradually starting to edge back up. It is not expected to be pushing the top of the target zone until mid to late 1998.
It was the better than expected moderation in inflation that gave the RBA the space to cut official interest rates three times in the second half of 1996 in the face of a stalling economy.

Whether or not there is another interest rate cut will probably be determined by events next week, but the inflation data does need to show continued moderation for a fourth cut to remain an option, economists said.
The final decision would also depend on the outcome of the U.S. policy setting FOMC meeting next week, and with the release of November quarter wages data on Thursday.
As well, some economists feel the RBA would hold off any decision until the outcome of the Australian Council of Trade Union's Living Wage claim in the next couple of months.
